editorial:
Imagine the shock when you see the modern 3D Turtles suddenly run into the classic 2D versions of themselves from the 80s. It is a wild ride that feels like a giant party for fans of all ages. You get to see two different versions of Leonardo, Raphael, Donatello, and Michelangelo trying to figure out why their worlds are merging. The vibe is totally laid-back and funny, focusing on the chemistry between the two groups as they realize they have the same quirks and loves for pizza, despite looking completely different. 

What really works here is the nostalgia and the fast-paced action. You will love how the movie handles the different art styles without it feeling weird. While the plot is pretty simple and some of the jokes might feel a bit childish, the heart of the story is great. If you are looking for a fun time, you should definitely grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection or look for it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best colors. It is a perfect pick for a family movie night or a trip down memory lane.
endingExplained: Everything wraps up when the two teams of Turtles finally track down the Technodrome. They work together to defeat the villains and close the portal that mixed their worlds. After a big fight, the classic Turtles have to head back to their own dimension before they are stuck forever. They say a heartfelt goodbye, realizing that no matter what they look like, they are all brothers. The worlds split apart, and everything goes back to normal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and old-school cartoons.
